title: Human papillomavirus 16 genomic variation in head and neck cancer: a systematic review with structural and functional annotation

analysis.scope_and_question: However, emerging evidence suggests that specific HPV16 genomic variants may be associated with poorer clinical outcomes.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The comprehensive mapping of HPV16 SNPs in HNC provides an important grounding for understanding how these SNPs may be associated with disease progression and patient outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: However, emerging evidence suggests that specific HPV16 genomic variants may be associated with poorer clinical outcomes. These SNPs were extracted and mapped to the HPV16 genome, while structural and functional characteristics were assessed using UniProt and the RCSB Protein Data Bank. The comprehensive mapping of HPV16 SNPs in HNC provides an important grounding for understanding how these SNPs may be associated with disease progression and patient outcomes. Although many of the identified SNPs are within important HPV16 regions, their associations with disease progression remain unclear. Further studies are required to determine which variants are associated with patient outcomes.

title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus and HPV vaccination among cisgender bisexual women: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: This paper proposes a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine whether reported HPV prevalence and vaccination rates among cisgender bisexual women differ based on whether bisexuality is defined by identity or behavior.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The protocol is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252015) and follows PRISMA-P guidelines.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Findings will clarify how operational definitions shape observed HPV-related outcomes and inform tailored cervical cancer prevention strategies for cisgender bisexual women.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Research on HPV prevalence and vaccination among cisgender bisexual women is limited and inconsistent.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Random-effects meta-analyses will estimate pooled HPV prevalence and vaccination rates by definition type.

analysis.summary_en: This paper proposes a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine whether reported HPV prevalence and vaccination rates among cisgender bisexual women differ based on whether bisexuality is defined by identity or behavior. The protocol is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252015) and follows PRISMA-P guidelines. Findings will clarify how operational definitions shape observed HPV-related outcomes and inform tailored cervical cancer prevention strategies for cisgender bisexual women. Research on HPV prevalence and vaccination among cisgender bisexual women is limited and inconsistent. Random-effects meta-analyses will estimate pooled HPV prevalence and vaccination rates by definition type.

title: Prevalence and distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes among women living with HIV in Nigeria

analysis.research_question_and_background: Women living with HIV (WLHIV) are at significantly higher risk of persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV), and consequently, cervical cancer. However, large scale data on the epidemiology of hrHPV genotypes among WLHIV are limited in Nigeria.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a cross-sectional study among 1327 WLHIV aged 25-60 years receiving HIV care from six selected Nigeria Implementation Science Alliance-Model Innovation and Research Centers (NISA-MIRCs) across Nigeria.
analysis.methods: Cervical swabs were obtained, and HPV DNA genotype was determined using the Hybribio Genoarray assay that detects 37 HPV genotypes including 14 high-risk HPVs. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected using interviewer-administered structured questionnaire. Factors independently associated with hrHPV infection were identified using multivariable logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Among the 1105 participants with analyzable samples, the overall HPV and hrHPV prevalence were 30.9% and 22.1%, respectively, with regional differences. Non-HPV 16 and 18 accounted for nearly two-thirds (67.6%) of hrHPV infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The top five most often detected hrHPVs were HPV-58 (14.2%), HPV-16 (12.7%), HPV-52 (12.4%), HPV-31 (10.6%), and HPV-18 (10.3%).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This multi-site study showed a significant and genotype-diverse burden of hrHPV among HIV-positive women in Nigeria, with most infections caused by non-HPV16/18 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In a multivariate analysis, ART usage for one year or less was associated with hrHPV infection (aOR = 8.2, 95% CI 4.3-16.0).

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) among women living with HIV (WLHIV) in Nigeria. A cross-sectional design was used, involving 1327 WLHIV aged 25-60 years from six centers across Nigeria. Cervical swabs were collected and HPV DNA genotypes were identified using the Hybribio Genoarray assay, which detects 37 HPV genotypes, including 14 high-risk types. Among 1105 participants with analyzable samples, the overall HPV and hrHPV prevalence were 30.9% and 22.1%, respectively, with regional differences. Non-HPV 16 and 18 accounted for nearly two-thirds (67.6%) of hrHPV infections, with the top five genotypes being HPV-58, HPV-16, HPV-52, HPV-31, and HPV-18. The study highlights the need for cervical cancer screening integration within HIV care and suggests the importance of HPV vaccines with broader coverage than just HPV 16 and 18. The findings are limited by the cross-sectional design and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and detailed analysis.

title: Concordance of flow cytometric E6/E7 mRNA detection with human papillomavirus DNA testing and cervical cytology in a cervical cancer screening cohort

analysis.research_question_and_background: Overexpression of viral oncogenes E6 and E7 of high-risk (HR)–human papillomavirus (HPV) plays a key role in the progression to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and cancer. Detection of E6/E7 mRNA may help distinguish between transient and transforming infections, thus improving cervical cancer screening accuracy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 526 women undergoing cervical cancer screening between January 2023 and May 2025 were enrolled. The study aimed to evaluate the association of E6/E7 mRNA expression with HR-HPV infection, cervical cytology, and histologically confirmed cervical lesions.
analysis.methods: E6/E7 mRNA expression was assessed using flow cytometry with the HPV OncoTect 3Dx E6/E7 mRNA assay and compared with HR-HPV DNA testing, cervical cytology, and available histopathologic findings from biopsy specimens.
analysis.main_results: Among 526 samples, eight (1.5%) tested positive for E6/E7 mRNA, compared to 30 (5.7%) HR-HPV DNA–positive and 17 (3.2%) abnormal cytology results. Median E6/E7 mRNA expression was higher in HR-HPV–positive cases and in cytologically abnormal cases. Almost perfect agreement was observed between E6/E7 mRNA results, HR-HPV DNA testing, and cytology.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Flow-cytometric E6/E7 mRNA detection showed high overall agreement with HPV DNA testing and cytology in this screening cohort. Histopathologic follow-up was available for nine women with cytological abnormalities ≥low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, including four CIN2 and five CIN1 cases.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that E6/E7 mRNA detection could be a valuable tool for improving the accuracy of cervical cancer screening. Larger prospective studies with comprehensive histologic follow-up are needed to determine its clinical utility.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the potential for missing histopathologic data. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single cohort with limited histologic follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the association of E6/E7 mRNA expression with high-risk HPV infection, cervical cytology, and histologically confirmed cervical lesions. It aimed to compare the agreement of E6/E7 mRNA detection with HPV DNA testing and cytology. Among 526 samples, 1.5% tested positive for E6/E7 mRNA, compared to 5.7% HR-HPV DNA–positive and 3.2% abnormal cytology results. Almost perfect agreement was observed between E6/E7 mRNA results, HR-HPV DNA testing, and cytology. The study found that E6/E7 mRNA detection showed high overall agreement with HPV DNA testing and cytology, suggesting its potential as a tool for improving cervical cancer screening accuracy. However, the study is limited by its retrospective design and the potential for missing histopathologic data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Esophageal Squamous Papillomas: Human Papillomavirus Association and Natural History

analysis.research_question_and_background: Esophageal squamous papillomas (ESPs) are rare epithelial lesions with an incompletely understood pathogenesis and uncertain malignant potential.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of histologically confirmed ESPs at Cleveland Clinic between January 2019 and July 2023.
analysis.methods: Clinical, endoscopic, and histopathologic data were collected. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue underwent RNA in situ hybridization (RNA ISH) targeting E6/E7 mRNA to detect transcriptionally active low- and high-risk HPV subtypes.
analysis.main_results: 184 ESP cases were identified, representing the largest single-center cohort. Lesions were predominantly solitary, small (<5 mm), and located in the mid-esophagus. No lesion demonstrated dysplasia, epidermoid metaplasia, or invasive carcinoma at index endoscopy. All evaluable lesions were negative for transcriptionally active HPV by RNA ISH (0/177; 95% CI, 0-2.1%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The absence of transcriptionally active HPV supports a limited role for HPV in ESP pathogenesis and does not support routine HPV testing in typical, non-dysplastic ESPs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our findings support the generally benign natural history of ESPs and highlight the need for prospective studies with standardized long-term surveillance to better define their malignant potential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Follow-up endoscopy was available in 70 patients (38%), with a median follow-up of 24 months and surveillance extending to ≥4 years. No dysplasia / malignant transformation was observed during available follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between esophageal squamous papillomas (ESPs) and human papillomavirus (HPV) to better understand their pathogenesis and malignant potential. A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Cleveland Clinic between January 2019 and July 2023, analyzing 184 ESP cases. Clinical, endoscopic, and histopathologic data were collected, and RNA in situ hybridization (RNA ISH) was used to detect transcriptionally active HPV subtypes. All evaluable lesions were negative for HPV (0/177; 95% CI, 0-2.1%). The study found that ESPs were predominantly solitary, small, and located in the mid-esophagus, with no evidence of dysplasia or malignant transformation. The authors concluded that HPV likely plays a limited role in ESP pathogenesis and that routine HPV testing is not necessary for typical, non-dysplastic ESPs. The study highlights the need for prospective research with standardized long-term surveillance to better define the malignant potential of ESPs. The evidence is moderate, as the study was limited by a relatively small follow-up cohort and potential biases in HPV detection methods.

title: Poliovirus receptor ( CD155 ) expression in gastric‐type adenocarcinoma of the cervix compared with human papillomavirus–associated and other human papillomavirus–independent adenocarcinomas

analysis.research_question_and_background: Gastric-type adenocarcinoma (GAS), a human papillomavirus-independent (HPVI) histological type of cervical adenocarcinoma, has a poorer prognosis and a distinct immune microenvironment compared with HPV-associated (HPVA) adenocarcinoma.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We retrospectively studied 142 patients with cervical adenocarcinoma (37 GAS, 92 HPVA and 13 HPVI [non-GAS] cases).
analysis.methods: PVR, PD-L1 (combined positive score [CPS] and tumour area positivity [TAP]) and CD8-positive tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes were quantified immunohistochemically.
analysis.main_results: PVR positivity (H-score ≥ 50) was present in all GAS cases (100%), versus 56.5% of HPVA and 69.2% of HPVI (non-GAS) cases and the PVR H-score differed significantly among groups, with the highest median in GAS (112.8 vs. 70.8 in HPVA and 98.2 in HPVI [non-GAS]; P 100) was associated with poorer overall and recurrence-free survival in univariable analysis (both P < 0.001), but this association was not maintained after adjustment for stage and histological group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: PVR expression was highest in GAS among the histological groups and correlated with PD-L1 scores (CPS and TAP) and aggressive clinicopathological features, but was not an independent prognostic marker after adjustment for stage and histology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support further investigation of PVR as a therapeutic target in GAS.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize the expression of the poliovirus receptor (PVR, CD155) in gastric-type adenocarcinoma (GAS) of the cervix compared with HPV-associated (HPVA) and other HPV-independent (HPVI) adenocarcinomas. The research found that PVR positivity was highest in GAS, with all cases showing H-score ≥ 50, compared to 56.5% of HPVA and 69.2% of HPVI (non-GAS) cases. The PVR H-score varied significantly among the groups, with the highest median in GAS. However, the association between PVR positivity and poorer survival was not maintained after adjusting for stage and histological group. The authors interpreted these findings as indicating that PVR expression is linked to aggressive clinicopathological features in GAS but is not an independent prognostic marker. The study's results suggest that PVR could be a potential therapeutic target in GAS, though the evidence is limited by the retrospective design and lack of detailed limitations.

title: Genetic and Epigenetic Determinants of Endometrial LIF Expression and the Potential Role of Human Papillomavirus E6-Mediated p53 Degradation

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the genetic and epigenetic factors influencing endometrial LIF expression and their potential connection to HPV E6-mediated p53 degradation, which could impact implantation and pregnancy outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research was a review of existing literature focusing on the mechanistic relationship between HPV E6, p53 degradation, and endometrial LIF expression, with an emphasis on human data and genetic associations.
analysis.methods: The study relied on a comprehensive review of genetic and epigenetic studies, including analysis of polymorphisms such as TP53 codon 72 and variations in LIF, MDM2, MDM4, and USP7 genes, as well as the role of HPV E6 in p53 degradation.
analysis.main_results: The review found that while the mouse model shows p53 regulation of LIF expression, human data support this relationship only through genetic evidence, not biochemical demonstration. Additionally, TP53 codon 72 polymorphism rs1042522 was linked to implantation failure in some cohorts but not in the largest study.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as suggesting a potential genetic link between HPV E6-mediated p53 degradation and endometrial LIF expression, though they emphasized the lack of direct biochemical evidence in humans.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future research on the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of HPV-related reproductive health issues, particularly in understanding how viral oncoproteins affect endometrial function and pregnancy outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on genetic associations rather than direct biochemical evidence in humans, and the mixed results of TP53 polymorphism suggest the need for further investigation. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the genetic and epigenetic determinants of endometrial LIF expression and their potential connection to HPV E6-mediated p53 degradation. While the mouse model demonstrates p53 regulation of LIF, human data only support this relationship through genetic evidence. The TP53 codon 72 polymorphism rs1042522 was associated with implantation failure in some cohorts but not in the largest study. The authors propose a mechanistic hypothesis linking HPV E6 to p53 degradation and its impact on endometrial function, though they note the lack of direct biochemical evidence. The findings may guide future research on HPV-related reproductive health issues, but the evidence is moderate due to the reliance on genetic associations and inconsistent results.

title: Human papillomavirus RNA in situ hybridisation in conjunctival papillary squamous cell carcinoma in situ

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterise conjunctival papillary squamous cell carcinoma in situ (pSCCis) and compare these findings with conjunctival papilloma, addressing the need to understand the role of human papillomavirus (HPV) in this condition.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A study was performed on pSCCis identified between 2015 and 2024, comparing them with a conjunctival papilloma cohort from the same period.
analysis.methods: HPV RNA in situ hybridisation (ISH) was performed on all pSCCis, and clinical and histopathologic data were collected and compared with the conjunctival papilloma cohort.
analysis.main_results: Twenty-four pSCCis were included, with 17 (71%) showing high-risk HPV, 5 (21%) showing low-risk HPV, and 2 (8%) being HPV-negative. High-risk HPV-positive pSCCis were more likely to feature loss of goblet cells and a well-defined transition between non-dysplastic and dysplastic epithelium compared to low-risk HPV-positive pSCCis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that high-risk HPV-positive pSCCis showed a transformative phenotype, while low-risk HPV-positive pSCCis showed a productive phenotype, overlapping with conjunctival papilloma.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HPV plays a significant role in pSCCis, with high-risk HPV-positive tumours showing a distinct phenotype. This could inform surveillance and diagnostic strategies for pSCCis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the small sample size and the lack of randomisation. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterised conjunctival papillary squamous cell carcinoma in situ (pSCCis) and found that high-risk HPV-positive pSCCis showed a transformative phenotype, while low-risk HPV-positive pSCCis showed a productive phenotype, overlapping with conjunctival papilloma. The findings suggest a significant role for HPV in pSCCis and could inform surveillance and diagnostic strategies.

title: Anal squamous cell carcinoma is predominantly driven by human papillomavirus infection across different geographic regions

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is considered the main etiological factor of anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC). However, it is not known whether there are geographical differences in terms of epidemiological features or prevalence of HPV infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aimed at comparing the etiopathogenic and epidemiological characteristics of ASCC in Mozambique and Spain, two countries with markedly different epidemiological backgrounds regarding HPV and human immunodeficiency virus infection. All ASCCs diagnosed in two tertiary referral hospitals from Mozambique and Spain between 2019–2023 were included.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for HPV-based screening and prevention strategies for anal cancer in both Mozambique and Spain, highlighting the importance of understanding regional variations in HPV-related disease patterns.

HPV16 was the most common type, but other HPV types were more frequently detected in the absence of HPV16 in Mozambique. The study also identified two distinct pathways for HPV-independent ASCC development. These findings underscore the importance of HPV in anal cancer etiology and suggest the need for targeted screening and prevention strategies. However, the study's focus on tertiary referral hospitals may limit its generalizability.

title: Presence of Human Papillomaviruses in the Normal-Appearing Hypopharyngeal Mucosa: A Prospective Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a well-established etiological factor in oropharyngeal cancer, whereas its role in the hypopharynx is less well understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective study investigated the prevalence of HPV in normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based HPV detection. Consecutive patients undergoing hypopharyngoscopy, laryngomicroscopy, or transnasal esophagogastroscopy for benign indications were prospectively recruited. Participants completed a questionnaire addressing HPV-related risk factors.
analysis.methods: Biopsies were obtained from normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa and analyzed for HPV DNA by PCR-based genotyping.
analysis.main_results: Tissue samples were collected from 53 patients (median age, 51 years; range, 18-85 years), of whom 32 (60.4%) were female. One sample was excluded because of insufficient DNA quality. Among the remaining 52 evaluable samples, one was positive for a cutaneous HPV type and one for high-risk HPV18. The HPV18-positive sample originated from a patient who was subsequently diagnosed with a p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma arising in a vallecular cyst. RNA in situ hybridization confirmed transcriptionally active HPV within the tumor. A history of HPV-associated benign disease was reported by 18 of 53 patients (34%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings provide novel data on HPV prevalence in the hypopharynx and suggest that oncogenic HPV may occasionally be present in clinically normal hypopharyngeal mucosa.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide novel data on HPV prevalence in the hypopharynx and suggest that oncogenic HPV may occasionally be present in clinically normal hypopharyngeal mucosa, which may inform future studies on HPV-associated malignancies in this region.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: HPV DNA detection was rare in normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa, even among individuals with a history of HPV-associated benign disease. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 4.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective study aimed to investigate the prevalence of human papillomavirus (HPV) in normal-appearing hypopharyngeal mucosa, as its role in the hypopharynx is less understood compared to oropharyngeal cancer. The study recruited consecutive patients undergoing procedures for benign indications and collected biopsies for HPV DNA analysis using PCR-based genotyping. Results showed that HPV was detected in only one of 52 evaluable samples, with one being high-risk HPV18. This HPV18-positive sample was linked to a subsequent diagnosis of p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma in a vallecular cyst, and RNA in situ hybridization confirmed active HPV transcription in the tumor. A history of HPV-associated benign disease was reported by 34% of participants. The findings suggest that oncogenic HPV may occasionally be present in clinically normal hypopharyngeal mucosa, providing novel insights into HPV prevalence in this region. However, the low detection rate and limited sample size indicate that the evidence is moderate in strength.

title: Pharmacological enhancement of 20S proteasome-mediated degradation exposes a vulnerability in human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven cervical cancer

analysis.research_question_and_background: Despite the availability of prophylactic vaccines against human papillomavirus (HPV), infection and subsequent cervical cancer remain a significant global health problem. The study aimed to explore new therapeutic strategies targeting HPV-driven oncogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the degradation of HPV viral oncoproteins E6 and E7, which drive oncogenesis through disruption of cell growth control pathways. It focused on high-risk strains of the virus and their association with cervical cancer.
analysis.methods: The researchers examined the degradation of HPV oncoproteins through the 20S proteasome, demonstrating that these proteins can be degraded in a ubiquitin-independent manner. They also assessed the impact of small molecule-enhancement of this protease on HPV E6 and E7 protein levels.
analysis.main_results: Whole cell proteomic analysis revealed remodeling of cancer-associated pathways, including shifts consistent with reduced proliferative and oncogenic metabolic signaling. The study showed that 20S proteasome activation suppressed HPV-driven phenotypes, such as reduced proliferation and restoration of cell-cycle regulatory signaling.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify a previously unrecognized vulnerability of HPV oncoproteins and suggest that 20S proteasome activation could be a potential therapeutic strategy for HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of new therapeutic approaches for HPV-associated cancers, particularly cervical cancer, by targeting the 20S proteasome pathway.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis. However, the findings are supported by proteomic analysis and demonstrate a clear, evidence-grounded mechanism.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores a novel therapeutic strategy for HPV-associated cervical cancer by targeting the 20S proteasome. It reveals that HPV oncoproteins E6 and E7 can be degraded through a ubiquitin-independent pathway, offering a potential vulnerability for intervention. The research highlights that small molecule-enhancement of the 20S proteasome reduces E6 and E7 protein levels, leading to suppression of HPV-driven phenotypes such as reduced proliferation and restored cell-cycle signaling. These findings suggest a previously unrecognized mechanism that could inform future therapeutic development. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis. The results are supported by proteomic analysis and demonstrate a clear, evidence-grounded mechanism, indicating moderate confidence in the findings.

title: A Community Engaged Feasibility Study of High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Self-Sampling for Cervical Cancer Screening in Sexual and Gender Minority People

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the acceptability and feasibility of at-home self-sampling cervical cancer screening (CCS) for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) in sexual and gender minority (SGM) Kentuckians.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted using virtual interviews with 19 participants in 2022–2023 to explore socioecological factors influencing cervical cancer screening and the feasibility of hrHPV self-sampling in SGM individuals.
analysis.methods: Criterion and snowball sampling were used to recruit participants, and data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic approach with team member consensus to identify salient themes.
analysis.main_results: Six overarching themes were identified: cervical cancer screening perceptions, prior negative healthcare experiences, desirability of hrHPV self-sampling, completing hrHPV self-sampling, concerns about hrHPV self-sampling, and reasons for study participation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that at-home hrHPV self-sampling is a promising intervention to increase cervical cancer screening in SGM people, highlighting the importance of culturally competent healthcare environments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that hrHPV self-sampling could be a valuable tool for improving cervical cancer screening rates among SGM individuals, potentially contributing to more equitable healthcare access.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its qualitative design and small sample size, but the evidence is strong due to the use of team member consensus and thematic analysis to identify salient themes.

analysis.summary_en: This study explored the acceptability and feasibility of at-home self-sampling for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) cervical cancer screening among sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals in Kentucky. Using virtual interviews with 19 participants, the research identified six key themes related to perceptions of cervical cancer screening, past negative healthcare experiences, and the desirability and concerns of hrHPV self-sampling. The authors concluded that hrHPV self-sampling is a promising intervention to increase screening rates in SGM populations, emphasizing the need for culturally competent healthcare environments. The study's qualitative design and small sample size limit its generalizability, but the thematic analysis and team consensus provide robust insights into the feasibility of this approach. These findings could inform future efforts to improve cervical cancer screening access for marginalized groups.

title: Preferential recruitment of PML isoform II by incoming HPV16 genome transport vesicles facilitates early stage of infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which human papillomavirus (HPV) targets promyelocytic leukemia nuclear bodies (PML NBs) to facilitate early transcription and replication, addressing a gap in understanding the specific interaction between HPV and PML NBs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using HeLa cells, where individual PML NB isoform and HPV16 minor protein, L2, over-expression experiments were performed to examine the interaction between HPV and PML NBs.
analysis.methods: The researchers used over-expression experiments in HeLa cells to study the interaction between PML NBs and HPV16, focusing on the recruitment of PML isoform II to incoming HPV genomes within transport vesicles.
analysis.main_results: The association of PML NBs with the HPV16 viral genome was observed to be transient and lost over time, indicating a dynamic interaction during the early stages of infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that PML II binds to the lipids of the HPV-harboring membrane-bound vesicles rather than the L2 protein, offering a novel insight into the mechanism of HPV targeting PML NBs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide important information for understanding the early stages of HPV infection and may inform future research on viral strategies for host cell manipulation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to HeLa cells and does not account for in vivo conditions, but the evidence is strong based on the observed transient association and lipid binding mechanism.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how human papillomavirus (HPV) interacts with promyelocytic leukemia nuclear bodies (PML NBs) to facilitate early infection. Using over-expression experiments in HeLa cells, the authors conclude that PML II binds to the lipids of the HPV-harboring vesicles rather than the L2 protein. The transient association of PML NBs with the HPV genome suggests a dynamic process during early infection. These findings offer a novel understanding of HPV's mechanism for targeting PML NBs, which may have implications for future research on viral strategies. However, the study is limited to in vitro conditions and does not account for in vivo factors, which may affect the generalizability of the results. title: Study on the molecular mechanism of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells inducing epithelial-mesenchymal transition in HPV-associated cervical cancer through activation of miR-129 .

analysis.research_question_and_background: HPV-associated cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death in women worldwide. The role of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and miR-129 in tumor progression remains unclear.

title: Prevalence and distribution of high-risk Human Papillomavirus Genotypes in Cervical cancer tissue biopsies at Bugando Medical Centre, Northwestern Tanzania

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, where the distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) genotypes varies geographically.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Data on hrHPV genotypes in cervical cancer tissue from northwestern Tanzania are limited. This study determined the prevalence and distribution of hrHPV genotypes in fresh cervical cancer tissue biopsies at Bugando Medical Centre, Mwanza, Tanzania.
analysis.methods: We conducted a hospital-based study among 309 women with histologically confirmed cervical cancer between January 2024 and January 2025. We tested fresh cervical tissue biopsies for hrHPV DNA using the AnyplexTM II HPV28 real-time PCR assay. We analysed clinical, demographic, and histopathological characteristics using chi-square and logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: We detected hrHPV DNA in 277/309 (89.6%) women. Genotype-level analyses accounted for clustering of multiple detections within women. Among women with known HIV status, HIV-positive status was associated with higher odds of HPV16/18 detection compared with other hrHPV genotypes (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.09–2.05; p = 0.013).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HrHPV positivity was higher in squamous cell carcinoma than adenocarcinoma (91.7% vs 83.7%; p = 0.044), but histological subtype was not independently associated with hrHPV positivity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and prevention strategies for HPV-associated cervical cancer in northwestern Tanzania.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its hospital-based design and potential for selection bias, but the evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of a validated PCR assay and statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) genotypes in cervical cancer tissue biopsies at Bugando Medical Centre in northwestern Tanzania. A hospital-based study was conducted among 309 women with histologically confirmed cervical cancer between January 2024 and January 2025, using the AnyplexTM II HPV28 real-time PCR assay to detect hrHPV DNA. The results showed that 89.6% of the women were hrHPV positive, with HPV16 being the most frequent genotype (36.7%), followed by HPV18 (21.9%). Among hrHPV-positive women, 69.0% had multiple-genotype infections. HIV-positive status was associated with higher odds of HPV16/18 detection compared with other hrHPV genotypes (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.09–2.05; p = 0.013). The study found that hrHPV positivity was higher in squamous cell carcinoma than adenocarcinoma, but histological subtype was not independently associated with hrHPV positivity. These findings can inform targeted surveillance and prevention strategies for HPV-associated cervical cancer in the region. The study is limited by its hospital-based design and potential for selection bias, but the evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of a validated PCR assay and statistical analysis.

title: HPV16 E6 promotes the proliferation of cervical cancer cells through the CPT1A/c-Myc positive feedback loop.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which HPV16 E6 promotes the proliferation of cervical cancer cells, addressing a gap in understanding the molecular pathways involved in HPV-associated carcinogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in vitro using cervical cancer cell lines, focusing on the role of HPV16 E6 in cellular proliferation without involving human or animal populations.
analysis.methods: The researchers used molecular biology techniques, including gene expression analysis and cell proliferation assays, to examine the interaction between HPV16 E6 and the CPT1A/c-Myc pathway.
analysis.main_results: The study found that HPV16 E6 significantly promotes cervical cancer cell proliferation through a positive feedback loop involving CPT1A and c-Myc, with specific molecular interactions observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as evidence of a novel regulatory mechanism by which HPV16 E6 enhances cancer cell growth, highlighting the importance of the CPT1A/c-Myc axis in this process.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings contribute to the understanding of HPV16's role in cervical cancer progression, potentially informing targeted therapeutic strategies for HPV-associated malignancies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro models, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions, and the evidence is based on a single cell line, reducing generalizability. The confidence in these findings is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how HPV16 E6 promotes cervical cancer cell proliferation through a positive feedback loop involving CPT1A and c-Myc. The research was conducted in vitro using cervical cancer cell lines, employing molecular biology techniques to analyze gene expression and cell growth. The main results demonstrate a significant enhancement of cell proliferation linked to the CPT1A/c-Myc pathway, suggesting a novel mechanism in HPV-associated carcinogenesis. The authors interpret these findings as highlighting the importance of this pathway in HPV16's oncogenic effects, which could inform future therapeutic strategies. However, the study's reliance on in vitro models limits its applicability to real-world scenarios, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the limited scope of the experimental setup.

title: The dentist as sentinel: HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, the limits of the oral examination, vaccine advocacy and diagnostic delay in United States men — an integrated narrative and scoping review with a National Interest perspective

analysis.scope_and_question: Oropharyngeal cancer caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) has become the most common HPV-attributable cancer in the United States, and its burden falls disproportionately on men. The dental visit is a strategic but underused point of contact for both early recognition and vaccine promotion.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: PubMed-indexed literature and official United States sources (CDC, NCHS, American Cancer Society, FDA, HHS and state legislatures) were examined up to October 2026. This integrated review combines a narrative synthesis of the epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic pathway and drivers of delay of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer with a scoping map of studies on dental professionals' knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding HPV vaccination and of policy initiatives that allow vaccine promotion or administration in dental settings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Incidence among men rose 2.7% per year between 2001 and 2017, regional-stage disease predominated, and men carry an oral HPV prevalence of 11.5% against 3.2% in women. The primary tumour is frequently invisible on routine inspection, and a painless neck mass is the most common first sign.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Fewer than one-third of surveyed dentists discuss the vaccine, yet more than half say they would administer it if allowed. Up-to-date adolescent HPV vaccination reached 63.4% in 2025, without improvement for four consecutive years, while 86.9% of children and 66.7% of adults report a dental visit in the past year.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: A sentinel framework for screening, referral and vaccine advocacy is proposed, together with education priorities for the dental workforce, and the national interest of the problem is set out. The study's limitations and suggestions for future research are discussed.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the rising burden of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer in the United States, particularly among men, and highlights the potential of dentists as sentinels for early detection and vaccine promotion. The review synthesizes epidemiological data, clinical features, and diagnostic challenges of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, alongside a scoping analysis of dental professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding HPV vaccination. It notes that while HPV vaccination rates among adolescents have stagnated, dental visits remain common, suggesting an opportunity for integrating vaccine advocacy into routine dental care. The review proposes a framework for dental professionals to engage in screening, referral, and vaccine promotion, emphasizing the need for education and policy changes to support this role. Despite the potential, the study finds that fewer than one-third of dentists discuss HPV vaccination, though more than half express willingness to administer it if permitted. The review concludes with a call for further research and action to address the gaps in HPV-related cancer prevention and management.

title: Covalent Ligands that Target the Human Papillomavirus E6 Oncoprotein.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for nonpeptidic functional binders targeting the HPV E6 oncoprotein, which is a key driver of several HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved screening a library of cysteine-reactive covalent ligands to identify potential inhibitors of the HPV E6 oncoprotein, focusing on its role in cancer progression.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed a library of cysteine-reactive covalent ligands to screen for functional binders, with a focus on the E6 protein's interaction with E6AP and its effect on p53 ubiquitination.
analysis.main_results: A pyrazoline hit, EN218, was identified, and further evaluation led to the development of (S)-WX48A, which stereoselectively reacted with C58 on E6 to inhibit E6-mediated p53 ubiquitination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that E6 can be directly and stereoselectively targeted with a covalent nonpeptidic small-molecule, offering a novel approach for developing more drug-like E6 inhibitors for HPV therapy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for the development of new therapeutic agents targeting HPV E6, which could lead to improved treatments for HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is still in an early stage and requires further medicinal chemistry optimization to achieve on-target cellular activity, indicating moderate confidence in the current findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study focuses on the development of covalent ligands targeting the human papillomavirus (HPV) E6 oncoprotein, a key driver of several HPV-associated cancers. The research aimed to identify nonpeptidic functional binders, as previous studies had explored peptidic inhibitors. A library of cysteine-reactive covalent ligands was screened, leading to the identification of a pyrazoline hit, EN218, and the subsequent development of (S)-WX48A, which stereoselectively binds to C58 on E6 to inhibit p53 ubiquitination. The findings suggest a novel approach for creating drug-like E6 inhibitors, potentially advancing HPV therapy. However, the molecule is still in an early stage and requires further optimization to achieve on-target cellular activity, limiting the current evidence strength to moderate.

title: Natural history of oral human papillomavirus among participants recruited through MSM-focused services in southwestern Kenya: an 18-month prospective cohort study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Oral human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA is associated with a subset of oropharyngeal cancers. This study aimed to characterise oral HPV prevalence, incidence, same-type persistence, and first non-detection, and examine associated factors among participants recruited through MSM-focused services in Kenya.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Between July and December 2023, we enrolled 398 adults through two key-population clinics in Kisumu County, Kenya, with equal numbers by HIV status. The study is an 18-month prospective cohort study focusing on participants recruited through MSM-focused services.
analysis.methods: Oral-rinse specimens were collected at baseline and at months 6, 12, and 18 and tested for HPV DNA by PCR with targeted high-risk genotyping.
analysis.main_results: Among 398 participants, oral HPV DNA prevalence was 7·8% at baseline, increased to 21·0% at month 12, and declined to 14·9% at month 18. The reported overall incidence rate was 82·0 per 1,000 person-months; there was no statistical evidence of a difference by HIV status (IRR 1·01, 95% CI 0·74–1·39), although the confidence interval was imprecise.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Receptive oral sex was associated with prevalent detection (aOR 2·78, 95% CI 1·17–6·42) and same-type persistence (aOR 4·14, 95% CI 1·48–11·87). These findings highlight the role of sexual behavior in oral HPV dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings motivate evaluation of inclusive HPV-vaccination strategies alongside HIV and sexual-health services, but do not alone establish vaccine effectiveness or justify a policy change.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The confidence interval for the incidence rate by HIV status was imprecise, and the study did not assess vaccine effectiveness or policy implications directly.

analysis.summary_en: This 18-month prospective cohort study in Kisumu County, Kenya, investigated the natural history of oral human papillomavirus (HPV) among adults recruited through MSM-focused services. The study aimed to characterise oral HPV prevalence, incidence, same-type persistence, and first non-detection, and examine associated factors. Oral-rinse specimens were collected at baseline and at months 6, 12, and 18 and tested for HPV DNA by PCR with targeted high-risk genotyping. Among 398 participants, oral HPV DNA prevalence was 7·8% at baseline, increased to 21·0% at month 12, and declined to 14·9% at month 18. The reported overall incidence rate was 82·0 per 1,000 person-months, with no statistical evidence of a difference by HIV status. Receptive oral sex was associated with prevalent detection and same-type persistence. These findings highlight the role of sexual behavior in oral HPV dynamics and motivate evaluation of inclusive HPV-vaccination strategies alongside HIV and sexual-health services. However, the confidence interval for the incidence rate by HIV status was imprecise, and the study did not assess vaccine effectiveness or policy implications directly.

title: Clinician Training, Text Messages, and Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Among Children Aged 10 to 12 Years

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of clinician communication training and parent-targeted text messages at increasing HPV vaccination among children aged 11 to 12 years. Importance was placed on the fact that HPV vaccination rates among adolescents remain below recommendations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a doubly randomized, 2-level nested clinical trial conducted from February 2022 to September 2024 among clinicians at 30 pediatric primary care clinics in Florida, children aged 10 to 12 years who had not received any of the 3 adolescent HPV vaccines, and their parents.
analysis.methods: Clinicians in the first 2 groups completed a 1-hour communication training and a 5-minute booster session. Patients within clinics were randomized 1:1:1 to 3 text message groups, aligned with the communication strategies: (1) bundled, (2) focused, and (3) no text messages. Analyses accounted for clinic-level clustering.
analysis.main_results: At baseline, 59 clinicians were included, with 17 randomized to the focused group, 21 to the bundled group, and 21 to the deferred group. The mean pre-post clinic-level difference for HPV vaccine initiation was 28.2 (95% CI, 25.3-31.1) percentage points and for completion was 16.1 (95% CI, 13.3-18.9) percentage points. Risk ratios for clinician training and text messaging did not differ between groups for initiation or completion. Among patients whose parents received text messages vs not, the risk ratio for initiation was 1.17 (95% CI, 1.08-1.26) and for completion was 1.29 (95% CI, 1.06-1.56).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that clinic-level HPV vaccination increased over time, but no differences in HPV vaccination by random assignment of clinician training or text messages were detected. When received, text messages were associated with higher HPV vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that parent-targeted text messages may be a useful tool to increase HPV vaccination rates among children aged 10 to 12 years, which could inform future public health strategies for improving vaccination coverage.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had a high confidence level as it was a randomized trial with a large sample size, but the lack of differences in vaccination rates by clinician training or text message groups may limit the strength of the evidence for these interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of clinician communication training and parent-targeted text messages in increasing HPV vaccination rates among children aged 10 to 12 years. Conducted in Florida, it involved 30 pediatric clinics and a large sample of children and parents. Clinicians were randomized into three training groups, while children were randomized into three text message groups. The results showed that clinic-level HPV vaccination increased over time, but no differences were detected between the training groups. Text messages were associated with higher vaccination rates. The study's design and large sample size support high confidence, though the lack of significant differences in the training groups may limit the strength of the evidence for those interventions.

title: Agreement and comparative performance of the MobiLab rapid oncoprotein E6/E7 antigen test and Cobas 4800 high-risk human papillomavirus deoxyribonucleic acid test for cervical cancer screening in a low-resource setting: a cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) accounts for approximately 97–99% of cervical cancer cases worldwide. Molecular assays that detect viral deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) are considered the gold standard for screening and early detection but remain inaccessible in many low-resource settings because of their cost and technical requirements.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted between February and July 2024 and included women who underwent cervical cancer screening at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital. In total, 257 women aged 30 years and older were randomly selected for this study.
analysis.methods: A cervical swab was obtained from all participants by healthcare providers for HR-HPV PCR DNA testing, followed by the collection of a cervical sample from all participants using the Delphi vaginal sampler for the MobiLab rapid oncoprotein E6/E7 antigen test. The Cobas 4800 assay is a qualitative, real-time PCR test that amplifies target sequences in the L1 region of the HR-HPV genome.
analysis.main_results: The overall positivity rate of the MobiLab rapid oncoprotein E6/E7 antigen test was 58.0% (149/257). Cross-tabulation of the MobiLab rapid oncoprotein E6/E7 antigen test and the Cobas 4800 HR-HPV DNA assay showed near-perfect agreement, with 148 of 149 positive results and 107 of 108 negative results classified similarly by both assays.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The two assays showed near-perfect agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.992; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.96–1.00; p < 0.001). Comparative performance analysis yielded a sensitivity of 99.33% (95% CI: 96.32–99.98%), a specificity of 99.07% (95% CI: 94.95–99.98%), a positive predictive value of 99.33% (95% CI: 95.46–99.90%), a negative predictive value of 99.07% (95% CI: 93.82–99.87%), and an AUC of 0.992 (95% CI: 0.979–1.000).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the MobiLab rapid oncoprotein E6/E7 antigen test could serve as a reliable alternative to DNA-based assays in low-resource settings for cervical cancer screening. Further studies incorporating cytological, colposcopic, and histopathological endpoints are needed to establish the clinical validity and determine the potential role of the MobiLab rapid oncoprotein E6/E7 antigen test in HPV screening programs in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study. The evidence strength is high as the study provides detailed agreement and performance metrics with statistical significance.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the agreement and performance of the MobiLab rapid oncoprotein E6/E7 antigen test and the Cobas 4800 HR-HPV DNA assay for cervical cancer screening in a low-resource setting. The study was conducted between February and July 2024 at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital, involving 257 women aged 30 years and older. The MobiLab test showed a positivity rate of 58.0%, and cross-tabulation revealed near-perfect agreement with the Cobas 4800 assay, with an overall agreement rate of 99.22% and a Cohen’s kappa coefficient of 0.992. The test demonstrated high sensitivity (99.33%) and specificity (99.07%), along with a high area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.992. These results suggest that the MobiLab test could be a viable alternative to DNA-based assays in low-resource settings for cervical cancer screening. However, further studies incorporating cytological, colposcopic, and histopathological endpoints are needed to confirm its clinical validity and role in HPV screening programs.

title: HPV16/18 Genotype and Histologic High-Grade Disease in Women with ASC-H Cytology: A Systematic Review of Genotype-Stratified Outcomes

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the association between HPV16/18 genotypes and histologic high-grade disease in women with ASC-H cytology. The central question is whether HPV16/18 genotypes can stratify the risk of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2+ (CIN2+).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes studies retrieved from PubMed and Europe PMC, searched on 1 October 2026 and updated on 7 October 2026. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and appraised studies using PRISMA 2020. Eligible studies provided ASC-H-specific histologic outcomes for HPV16/18-defined and comparator groups. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and certainty was rated with GRADE.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled risk ratio for high-grade outcomes in HPV16/18 versus other hrHPV types was 1.19 (95% CI, 0.94–1.49), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 64.9%) and a wide prediction interval (0.70–2.01). The results varied with study selection and genotype definition. In four studies with at least 30 hrHPV-negative women, high-grade outcomes occurred in 6.8–18.4%, and HPV-negative carcinomas were reported. Leave-one-out, screening context, and verification-restricted analyses did not show a consistent difference. The findings are consistent with current guidance for colposcopic evaluation of all ASC-H without genotype-based deferral.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence shows substantial heterogeneity and a wide prediction interval, indicating uncertainty in the pooled estimate. The risk of bias was limited by incomplete verification, confounding by age and screening context, heterogeneous assays and populations, and inaccessible reports. Certainty was very low for both outcomes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to clarify the incremental risk difference between HPV16/18 and other hrHPV types. Surveillance and diagnostic methods should account for the heterogeneity in assays and populations. The findings support current practices of colposcopic evaluation for all ASC-H cases without relying on genotype-based deferral.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the association between HPV16/18 genotypes and histologic high-grade disease in women with ASC-H cytology. The review included 16 studies with 1655 women, comparing HPV16/18 with other high-risk HPV types. The pooled risk ratio was 1.19 (95% CI, 0.94–1.49), with substantial heterogeneity and a wide prediction interval. The results varied with study selection and genotype definition, and leave-one-out analyses did not show consistent differences. The findings suggest that other hrHPV types and negative hrHPV results do not exclude high-grade disease, supporting current guidance for colposcopic evaluation without genotype-based deferral. Limitations include incomplete verification, confounding factors, and heterogeneous assays, leading to very low certainty for both outcomes.

title: Human Papillomavirus Genotype Distribution and Co-Infection Patterns in Clinically Selected Iraqi Women: A Cross-Sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes is the principal etiological factor in cervical carcinogenesis. However, HPV genotype distribution and co-infection patterns differ across populations and clinical settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this cross-sectional study, 100 clinically selected women attending clinics in Ramadi and Baghdad, Iraq (December 2025–July 2026), each contributed one specimen, collected by swab or superficial lesion scraping from a cervical, vulval, anal, or perianal site based on clinical assessment.
analysis.methods: HPV genotyping was performed by polymerase chain reaction followed by microarray hybridization, targeting 35 HPV genotypes.
analysis.main_results: HPV DNA was detected in 65 of 100 women (65.0%; 95% confidence interval, 55.3–73.6%). Of these, 48 had low-risk (LR)-only, 9 high-risk/potentially high-risk (HR/PHR)-only, and 8 mixed LR/HR/PHR infections. title: Baseline erythrocyte folate and outcomes of low grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia in a prospective cohort

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to examine the association between baseline erythrocyte folate and reversal, persistence, and progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1).
analysis.study_design_and_population: This community-based prospective cohort included 564 Chinese women with CIN1, with follow-up assessments at 6, 12, and 24 months.
analysis.methods: Baseline erythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay. Analyses included Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.
analysis.main_results: Among the 453 women assessed at 24 months, 342 (75.5%) had reversal, 58 (12.8%) had persistence, and 53 (11.7%) had progression to CIN2+. Lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with the composite adverse outcome in the reported adjusted model (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 2.42, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.62–3.61).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for the covariates included in the reported model.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that baseline erythrocyte folate levels may have prognostic value for CIN1 outcomes, potentially informing future studies on nutritional interventions for HPV-related diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Event-time assumptions and residual confounding limit interpretation. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between baseline erythrocyte folate levels and the outcomes of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1) in a community-based prospective cohort of 564 Chinese women. Baseline folate was measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, and follow-up assessments were conducted at 6, 12, and 24 months. The main results showed that lower folate levels were linked to a higher risk of adverse outcomes, including persistence and progression to CIN2+. The authors interpreted these findings as an association, noting that the results were adjusted for covariates. The study's significance lies in its potential to inform future research on the role of folate in HPV-related cervical diseases. However, limitations such as event-time assumptions and residual confounding affect the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

title: Genomic profiling of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma by human papillomavirus status in an Asian cohort: the TCOG T1322 registry study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the genomic profiles of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) in an Asian cohort, as HPV-positive and HPV-negative OPSCC are biologically distinct entities with different clinical behaviors and therapeutic responses. The research was needed because genomic studies of OPSCC have largely focused on Western populations, leaving the molecular landscape in Asian patients incompletely defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a multicenter tissue-based next-generation sequencing registry study (TCOG T1322; NCT05522881) conducted in Taiwan, enrolling patients with pathologically confirmed head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The study included 290 patients with OPSCC, of whom 190 had HPV-positive tumors and 100 had HPV-negative tumors.
analysis.methods: Tumor samples were subjected to comprehensive genomic profiling using a 440-gene targeted panel. Genomic alterations, pathway dysregulation, mutational signatures, tumor mutational burden (TMB), and therapeutic actionability were analyzed based on p16-defined HPV status.
analysis.main_results: Among the 290 patients with OPSCC, 190 had HPV-positive tumors and 100 had HPV-negative tumors. HPV-positive tumors frequently harbored alterations in PIK3CA (37%), BCL6 (14%), and immune checkpoint ligand amplifications CD274/PDCD1LG2 (6%). HPV-negative tumors were enriched for TP53 mutations (89%), CDKN2A deletions (34%), FAT1 alterations (33%), and CCND1 amplifications (30%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the distinct genomic profiles of HPV-positive and HPV-negative OPSCC in an Asian cohort, providing insights into their biological heterogeneity and identifying potential translational therapeutic targets for further investigation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results contribute to the understanding of the molecular differences between HPV-positive and HPV-negative OPSCC in Asian populations, which may inform more targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for this specific demographic.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on an Asian cohort, which may affect the generalizability of findings to other populations. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on genomic profiling of a specific cohort without broader validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the genomic profiles of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) in an Asian cohort, distinguishing between HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors. It enrolled 290 patients with pathologically confirmed head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Taiwan, using a 440-gene targeted panel for comprehensive genomic profiling. Results showed that HPV-positive tumors had frequent alterations in PIK3CA, BCL6, and immune checkpoint ligands, while HPV-negative tumors were enriched for TP53 mutations, CDKN2A deletions, FAT1 alterations, and CCND1 amplifications. The findings suggest distinct biological features of HPV-positive and HPV-negative OPSCC in this population, offering potential insights for targeted therapies. However, the study's focus on an Asian cohort may limit its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the specific context and lack of broader validation.

title: Survival in patients with a high prevalence of human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal cancer: real-world data from a national referral public hospital in South America

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate survival outcomes in patients with human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal cancer, as the incidence of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is rising globally.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at the National Cancer Institute of Chile, including patients with non-metastatic disease treated with curative intent between 2012 and 2023. A total of 146 patients were analysed; 75.3% were male, with a mean age of 60.7 years.
analysis.methods: Univariate and multivariate analyses (MVA) were conducted with logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards regression. HPV positivity (p16+) was detected in 62.3% of patients.
analysis.main_results: The 5-year overall survival was 60.9% [95% confidence interval (CI): 52.7–70.3]. p16+ [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.36; 95% CI: 0.19–0.68; p < 0.01] was independently associated with improved survival, whereas a smoking history of ≥ 10 pack-years (HR = 2.18; p = 0.02) and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) 2–4 (HR = 3.30; p < 0.01) were linked to worse outcomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that survival outcomes in this South American population, with a high prevalence of HPV-associated OPSCC, were comparable to internationally published data. In exploratory analyses, HPV association and concurrent chemotherapy were associated with better survival outcomes, with no significant differences between cisplatin schedules.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform clinical practice and treatment strategies for HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, particularly regarding the role of concurrent chemotherapy and the impact of patient characteristics on survival outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias. The evidence is moderate as it is based on observational data rather than randomized trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated survival outcomes in patients with human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal cancer treated at the National Cancer Institute of Chile between 2012 and 2023. A total of 146 patients were included, with 62.3% testing positive for HPV (p16+). The 5-year overall survival rate was 60.9% [95% CI: 52.7–70.3]. p16+ was independently associated with improved survival, while smoking history and ECOG performance status were linked to worse outcomes. The authors concluded that survival outcomes in this South American population were comparable to international data. The study is a retrospective cohort study, which limits the strength of the evidence to moderate.

title: Vaginal microecological characteristics in women across different age, maternal and disease states and their correlation with HPV infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate variations in vaginal microecology across female populations, elucidate alterations in vaginal microecology across age groups and physiological states, and provide evidence to support clinical prevention, diagnosis and treatment of vaginal diseases to safeguard women's reproductive health.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 200 women who underwent routine health check-ups at the Third Affiliated Hospital of Jinzhou Medical University between March and September 2024 were enrolled. Subjects were divided into five age groups (21-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, ≥60 years), a pregnant/postpartum group and a non-pregnant/non-postpartum group, and further categorized into a vaginal disease group and a healthy group within the same age group.

title: Prevalence and risk factors for human papillomavirus infection among women living with HIV in Sierra Leone: A cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer, a malignancy affecting the cervix, is the fourth most common cancer and cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. This burden disproportionately affects low-resource regions, where approximately 90% of cases occur.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors of high-risk HPV infection among women living with HIV (WLHIV) attending Connaught Hospital in Sierra Leone.
analysis.methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study of women living with HIV aged 25-65 years attending the HIV clinic at Connaught Teaching Hospital in Freetown between September and December 2024. Endocervical swabs were collected for HPV DNA testing. Data was analyzed using R (v4.4.0). Logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent risk factors for HPV positivity.
analysis.main_results: A total of 191 WLHIV were enrolled. High-risk HPV DNA was detected in 60 (31.4%) (95% CI 25.3%-38.3%) participants, with 50% (30/60) having multiple serotypes. The most common genotype was HPV 52, followed by 16 and 51. Only 30% of HPV-positive women had genotypes 16 or 18, targeted by the bivalent vaccine. On multivariable analysis, former contraceptive use was independently associated with increased HPV positivity (aOR=4.86, 95% CI: 1.65-17.37, p = 0.0032).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The high prevalence of high-risk HPV infection and predominance of non 16/18 genotypes among WLHIV in Sierra Leone underscore the need to integrate HPV screening within HIV services and consider broader HPV vaccine coverage in Sierra Leone.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of integrating HPV screening into HIV care and suggest the need for broader HPV vaccine coverage in Sierra Leone to address the specific genotypes prevalent among WLHIV.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the potential for confounding factors. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single study conducted in a specific setting.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence and risk factors of high-risk HPV infection among women living with HIV in Sierra Leone. It found that 31.4% of participants had high-risk HPV DNA, with HPV 52 being the most common genotype. Former contraceptive use was identified as an independent risk factor for HPV positivity. The study emphasizes the need for integrating HPV screening into HIV services and expanding vaccine coverage to address the prevalent genotypes. However, the findings are based on a single study in a specific setting, limiting their generalizability and suggesting moderate evidence strength.

title: Barriers and facilitators to HPV vaccination among adult men: A systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis

analysis.scope_and_question: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is widespread and a leading cause of preventable cancers, yet HPV vaccination uptake among adult men remains suboptimal.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Ten electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, and PsycINFO, were searched from inception to December 2025 using controlled vocabulary and free-text terms. Thematic synthesis followed Thomas and Harden's approach, with findings organized across five SEM levels.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Key barriers included gendered perceptions of HPV, low perceived susceptibility, stigma and disclosure concerns, provider communication failures, economic constraints, and structural access challenges. Facilitators included provider recommendation, supportive relationships, integrated care pathways, and health information access.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence base was concentrated among sexual minority men, sex workers, and healthcare-engaged men, with fewer studies among general male populations; six of the ten studies were conducted in the United States, limiting generalizability to adult men more broadly. Health service evaluation identified gaps between needs, resources, and utilization, particularly outside preventive care.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings highlight that improving HPV vaccination among adult men requires multilevel behavioral strategies alongside healthcare system improvements that better recognize and respond to men's vaccination needs.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis aimed to identify barriers and facilitators to HPV vaccination among adult men, guided by the Social Ecological Model (SEM). The review included ten studies from four countries, focusing on factors influencing vaccination decisions and healthcare responses. Key barriers were gendered perceptions, low perceived susceptibility, stigma, provider communication failures, economic constraints, and structural access challenges. Facilitators included provider recommendations, supportive relationships, integrated care pathways, and health information access. The evidence base was limited to specific populations, with fewer studies on general male populations and a concentration in the United States. Health service evaluation revealed gaps between men's vaccination needs, available resources, and service utilization, particularly outside preventive care. The findings suggest that improving HPV vaccination among adult men requires multilevel behavioral strategies and healthcare system reforms to better address their needs.

title: HPV vaccination initiation among preadolescents in Veneto, Italy: associations with chronic conditions and socioeconomic disadvantage

analysis.scope_and_question: Identifying population groups with lower human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination uptake is essential for developing targeted public health interventions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from Pedianet, an Italian primary-care pediatric database. Associations with sex, birth cohort, selected chronic conditions, disability, income-based healthcare exemption, and pediatric healthcare utilization were assessed using multivariable multilevel logistic regression, with a random intercept for family pediatrician.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV vaccination initiation was associated with health-related and sociodemographic factors. Among 19,245 children followed by 93 pediatricians, 53.6% received at least one HPV vaccine dose. Asthma was associated with higher odds of vaccination initiation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.36; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.12-1.67), whereas disability (aOR 0.71; 95% CI 0.58-0.88), income-based healthcare exemption (aOR 0.81; 95% CI 0.76-0.86), and male sex (aOR 0.79; 95% CI 0.74-0.84) were associated with lower odds of initiation. Associations with receipt of two HPV vaccine doses within the same age window were broadly consistent with those for initiation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Further research should clarify the barriers underlying these associations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Lower uptake among children with administratively recognized disability, those with income-based healthcare exemptions, and boys identifies groups that may benefit from targeted vaccination support.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates HPV vaccination initiation among preadolescents in the Veneto Region of Italy, focusing on associations with chronic conditions and socioeconomic disadvantage. Using data from Pedianet, a primary-care pediatric database, a retrospective cohort study was conducted to assess factors such as sex, birth cohort, chronic conditions, disability, income-based healthcare exemption, and pediatric healthcare utilization. The analysis employed multivariable multilevel logistic regression with a random intercept for family pediatrician. Among 19,245 children, 53.6% received at least one HPV vaccine dose. Asthma was linked to higher vaccination initiation, while disability, income-based healthcare exemption, and male sex were associated with lower initiation. The findings suggest that targeted support may be needed for children with disability, those with income-based healthcare exemptions, and boys. The study highlights the need for further research to understand the barriers behind these associations.
