title: Longitudinal methylation analysis for risk stratification of CIN2 lesions by HPV genotype

analysis.research_question_and_background: There is an urgent need for biomarkers that can distinguish regressive from progressive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) lesions to improve risk stratification in cervical cancer screening programs and avoid overtreatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study included 122 women (aged 18–30) with histologically confirmed CIN2 enrolled in an active surveillance trial at Helsinki University Hospital, Finland (ISRCTN91953024). Patients were monitored every 6 months for up to 24 months with cytology, HPV genotyping, and colposcopy.
analysis.methods: S5 methylation levels (pyrosequencing) were compared between women who regressed to normal histology (n = 89) and those who progressed to CIN3+ (n = 22, including one microinvasive cancer) or had persistent CIN2 (n = 11). Analysis was stratified based on baseline HPV genotypes.
analysis.main_results: The baseline S5 classifier significantly predicted progression/persistence with an odds ratio (OR) of 1.15 (95%CI 1.05–1.25). When excluding HPV16/18, the S5 classifier demonstrated a similar, borderline predictive association (OR 1.19; 95%CI 1.00–1.41), whereas cytology and HPV genotyping did not.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The S5 classifier showed potential as a prognostic triage biomarker for identifying progression in untreated CIN2, including cases with non-HPV16/18 types.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our exploratory findings suggest that elevated methylation levels may precede histological progression by up to 18 months.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As HPV16/18 prevalence declines, host-viral methylation panels may offer improved risk stratification compared to standard triage, though larger prospective studies in vaccinated populations are needed to confirm these findings and establish clinical utility.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the longitudinal performance of the S5 methylation classifier in predicting the clinical trajectory of untreated CIN2 across different HPV genotype groups. The research focused on identifying biomarkers to improve risk stratification in cervical cancer screening programs and avoid overtreatment. The study included 122 women with histologically confirmed CIN2 enrolled in an active surveillance trial at Helsinki University Hospital, Finland, and monitored them every 6 months for up to 24 months with cytology, HPV genotyping, and colposcopy. S5 methylation levels were compared between women who regressed to normal histology and those who progressed to CIN3+ or had persistent CIN2. The results showed that the S5 classifier significantly predicted progression/persistence with an odds ratio of 1.15 (95%CI 1.05–1.25). When excluding HPV16/18, the S5 classifier demonstrated a similar, borderline predictive association (OR 1.19; 95%CI 1.00–1.41), whereas cytology and HPV genotyping did not. The authors concluded that the S5 classifier has potential as a prognostic triage biomarker for identifying progression in untreated CIN2, including cases with non-HPV16/18 types. The findings suggest that elevated methylation levels may precede histological progression by up to 18 months. However, the authors emphasized the need for larger prospective studies in vaccinated populations to confirm these findings and establish clinical utility.

title: Health Economic Impact and Cost Threshold for Switching From Bivalent to Nonavalent HPV Vaccination for Preadolescent Girls in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa: A Mathematical Modeling Analysis Accounting for the HIV Epidemic

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the potential health economic impact of switching from bivalent to nonavalent HPV vaccination for preadolescent girls in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa, and to determine the cost threshold for such a switch.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mathematical modeling analysis was conducted using a validated compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model parameterized to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, simulating scenarios of 2vHPV and 9vHPV implementation over 100 years with varying coverage rates and vaccine efficacy assumptions.
analysis.methods: The study used a compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model parameterized to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, to simulate the implementation of 2vHPV and 9vHPV over 100 years with different coverage rates and vaccine efficacy assumptions, including lifelong or waning single-dose efficacy.
analysis.main_results: Single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert 7.9% more cervical cancer cases and 6.4% more deaths than 2vHPV (lifelong efficacy). The maximum 9vHPV price to be cost-effective ranged from $15 to $45/dose, depending on the willingness-to-pay threshold. At current market costs, single-dose 9vHPV at 90% coverage exceeded commonly used cost-effective thresholds with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios of $10,480/DALY averted (lifelong efficacy) and $8806/DALY averted (waning efficacy).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that implementing 9vHPV could result in a greater reduction in cervical cancer burden than 2vHPV, but they emphasized that vaccine costs need to be reduced for 9vHPV to be cost-effective in KwaZulu-Natal.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health decision-making regarding HPV vaccination strategies in South Africa, particularly in considering cost-effectiveness and the potential benefits of switching to 9vHPV.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a mathematical model, which may have limitations in capturing real-world complexities, and the evidence is abstract-only, which may affect the strength of the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the health economic impact and cost threshold for switching from bivalent to nonavalent HPV vaccination for preadolescent girls in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa. Using a validated compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model, the researchers simulated scenarios of 2vHPV and 9vHPV implementation over 100 years with varying coverage rates and vaccine efficacy assumptions. The results indicate that single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert more cervical cancer cases and deaths than 2vHPV, but current market costs exceed commonly used cost-effectiveness thresholds. The authors conclude that implementing 9vHPV could reduce cervical cancer burden more effectively than 2vHPV, but vaccine costs need to be reduced for it to be cost-effective. The study's findings are based on a mathematical model and are limited by the abstract-only evidence, which may affect the strength of the conclusions.

title: Association of Cannabis Use and Risks of Oral Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: Oral cancer is a major health concern globally, with its etiology linked to factors such as tobacco use, alcohol consumption, and HPV infection. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the association between cannabis use and the risk of developing oral cancer.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science to identify studies up to August 15, 2025. Inclusion criteria encompassed adult participants and observational studies on cannabis use and oral cancer risk. Meta-analysis utilized random-effects models to compute pooled odds ratios (ORs) in R software version 4.4. Newcastle Ottawa scale was used for quality assessment.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: From 1,063 records, 11 studies met the inclusion criteria with a total sample size of 245,594 participants. The meta-analysis revealed a pooled OR of 0.481 (95% CI: 0.306 to 0.757), suggesting a potential reduced risk of oral cancer with cannabis use, particularly noted in case-control studies (pooled OR: 0.455, 95% CI: 0.291 to 0.713). However, cohort study showed no significant association (pooled OR: 2.51, 95% CI: 0.244 to 25.823), and high heterogeneity was observed across studies. Current evidence does not support cannabis use as an independent risk factor for oral cancer.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Although some case-control studies suggested an inverse association, this finding was not supported by cohort studies and should be interpreted cautiously given the substantial heterogeneity and potential for residual confounding. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify this relationship.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the relationship between cannabis use and oral cancer risk. This review highlights the need for more research to address the heterogeneity observed in the studies and to better understand the mechanisms underlying the potential inverse association.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between cannabis use and oral cancer risk. From 11 studies, a pooled OR of 0.481 suggested a reduced risk, but cohort studies showed no significant association. Further research is needed to clarify the relationship and address heterogeneity.

title: Pre-implementation assessment of upstream domains on the uptake of HPV self-sampling in safety-net settings: a scoping review.

analysis.scope_and_question: This scoping review focuses on the barriers and facilitators of implementing HPV self-sampling in safety net settings, with an emphasis on upstream factors not yet explored in current research. The review examines the role of safety net providers and leadership in the uptake of HPV self-sampling tests, which are FDA-approved and aimed at mitigating cervical cancer screening disparities.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines to conduct a literature search, including peer-reviewed publications and grey literature. The findings were organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research to structure the analysis of implementation factors.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review found that safety net practices are capable of implementing HPV self-sampling by utilizing existing workflows and team members. However, external guidelines and policies significantly influence the implementation process, potentially delaying uptake in these settings.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is a lack of comprehensive research on the upstream factors affecting the implementation of HPV self-sampling in safety net settings. Additionally, the review highlights that while recent guideline endorsements and insurance coverage address some barriers, further research is needed to understand the full impact of these changes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Post-approval implementation research in safety net settings is an urgent priority, as recent guideline endorsements and insurance coverage are expected to reduce some of the barriers to HPV self-sampling uptake. This research should focus on understanding the specific challenges and facilitators within these settings to improve equitable access to cervical cancer screening.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review evaluates the implementation of HPV self-sampling in safety net settings, focusing on upstream factors influencing its uptake. The review highlights that while safety net practices can integrate HPV self-sampling into existing workflows, external guidelines and policies significantly impact the process. Recent endorsements and insurance coverage have begun to address some barriers, but further research is needed to fully understand the implementation landscape. The findings emphasize the importance of post-approval research to enhance equitable access to cervical cancer screening in these settings.

title: U.S. state-level variation in caregiver-reported provider recommendation of HPV vaccination to 13-to-17-year-old adolescents

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to examine state-level differences in provider recommendation of HPV vaccines among adolescents in the United States, as regional variations in such recommendations have been documented but limited research has focused on state-level variation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted using data from the National Immunization Survey–Teen (2023), analyzing caregiver-reported provider recommendations for HPV vaccines among 13-to-17-year-old adolescents across U.S.
analysis.methods: Multivariable logistic regression was used to model state-specific variations in provider recommendation of HPV vaccine, and proportion estimation was employed to examine state-specific prevalence.
analysis.main_results: Provider recommendation varied considerably across states, with lower odds of reporting a recommendation in Arkansas (AOR = 0.56, 95% CI = 0.33 to 0.96), Georgia (AOR = 0.49, 95% CI = 0.26 to 0.93), and Mississippi (AOR = 0.42, 95% CI = 0.24 to 0.74), and higher odds in New Hampshire (AOR = 2.40, 95% CI = 1.23 to 4.68) compared with California. Greater heterogeneity was observed in the South compared with other regions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the variability in HPV vaccine recommendation practices across U.S. states, suggesting that targeted interventions may be necessary to address disparities in vaccination rates.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform public health strategies to improve HPV vaccination rates by identifying states with low recommendation rates and implementing focused interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on caregiver-reported data, which may introduce bias, and the evidence is limited to state-level variations without further exploration of underlying factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated state-level differences in health care provider recommendations for HPV vaccination among 13-to-17-year-old adolescents in the United States. Using data from the National Immunization Survey–Teen (2023), the researchers found considerable variation in recommendation rates across states, with lower odds in Arkansas, Georgia, and Mississippi, and higher odds in New Hampshire compared to California. The findings indicate greater heterogeneity in the South, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions to improve HPV vaccine recommendations in states with lower rates. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on caregiver-reported data may introduce bias, limiting the strength of the evidence. These results can inform public health efforts to address disparities in HPV vaccination practices at the state level.

title: Narrative and Linguistic Strategies in HPV Vaccine Communication: A Content Analysis of Government, Medical Institutions, and Practitioners’ Accounts on Sina Weibo

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on the narrative and linguistic strategies used in HPV vaccine communication on Sina Weibo, examining how these strategies influence audience engagement. The central question is how different combinations of message features, such as narrative presence, perspective, grammatical mood, and linguistic modality, relate to engagement levels with HPV vaccine posts.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employs a narrative content analysis approach, using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis to identify configurations of message features associated with engagement. The study analyzed 638 HPV vaccine posts from government, medical institutions, and practitioners on Sina Weibo, focusing on narrative forms, linguistic modality, and account type.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The analysis found that posts from medical institutions using second-person, third-person, or impersonal narrative forms with high-modality language (i.e., language with high certainty) were associated with stronger audience engagement. Additionally, medical practitioners' posts that encouraged a conversational orientation through question-only formats also showed high engagement. In contrast, non-narrative declarative posts with medium-modality language from medical practitioners were linked to low engagement.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights that tentative, low-modality language was characteristic of three of the five low-engagement configurations, indicating a potential gap in understanding how different linguistic styles affect engagement. The findings also suggest that the effectiveness of narrative and linguistic strategies may depend on the source type and message content, but the exact mechanisms remain underexplored.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The results provide practical insights for designing more engaging HPV vaccine communication on social media. They emphasize the importance of using high-modality language and appropriate narrative forms when disseminating information from medical institutions, while also suggesting that conversational formats may be effective for practitioners. These findings can inform future strategies for improving public health messaging related to HPV vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how narrative and linguistic strategies in HPV vaccine communication on Sina Weibo influence audience engagement. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, the study identifies configurations of message features, such as narrative form and linguistic modality, that correlate with high or low engagement. Posts from medical institutions using high-modality language and various narrative forms showed stronger engagement, while non-narrative declarative posts with medium-modality language were associated with lower engagement. The findings suggest that message design should consider both the source type and the linguistic style to enhance vaccine communication effectiveness. The study also highlights gaps in understanding the precise mechanisms behind engagement differences and offers actionable insights for improving public health messaging.

title: Colposcopic magnified scanning-assisted CO 2 laser treatment (CMSLT) for vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (VaHSIL): A single-center prospective cohort study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of Colposcopic Magnified Scanning Laser Treatments (CMSLT) for patients with vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (vaHSIL), a rare condition associated with persistent high-risk HPV infection and potential progression to invasive carcinoma.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center prospective non-randomized cohort study was conducted between January 2022 and June 2024 on 63 patients with histologically confirmed vaHSIL. Patients were assigned to either the CMSLV group (n = 22) or the CMSLE group (n = 41) based on the 2011 IFCPC colposcopic terminology.
analysis.methods: The outpatient protocol utilized a laser system implemented with a computerized surgical scanner-assisted micromanipulator. The two-year follow-up included semi-annual screenings with HPV testing, cytology, and colposcopy.
analysis.main_results: The cumulative recurrence risk for vaHSIL was 14.5%, with no statistically significant difference between the two modalities. The CMSLE group showed a higher 2-year disease-free survival rate (70% vs. The progression rate to invasive carcinoma was 1.6% (1 case in the CMSLE cohort), revealing a 2.4% rate of occult cancer missed at initial colposcopic assignment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as suggesting that CMSLT may represent a feasible approach since it was safe, effective, and associated with patient compliance. The precision of the scanner-assisted technology minimizes thermal damage and the risk of undertreating occult cancer, allowing for tailored and efficient therapy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of standardized treatment protocols for vaHSIL, particularly in the context of HPV-associated diseases, by highlighting the potential benefits of scanner-assisted laser treatments in improving disease-free survival and reducing the risk of occult cancer.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is non-randomized, which may introduce bias, and the follow-up period was limited to two years. The evidence strength is moderate due to the study's design and the relatively small sample size.

analysis.summary_en: This single-center prospective cohort study evaluated the feasibility of Colposcopic Magnified Scanning Laser Treatments (CMSLT) for vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (vaHSIL), a rare condition linked to high-risk HPV infection. The study included 63 patients divided into two groups based on colposcopic terminology. CMSLT was performed using a computerized surgical scanner-assisted micromanipulator, with follow-up involving semi-annual screenings. The cumulative recurrence risk was 14.5%, with no significant difference between the two treatment modalities. However, the CMSLE group showed a higher disease-free survival rate. The progression to invasive carcinoma was 1.6%, with a 2.4% rate of occult cancer missed at initial diagnosis. Only one major complication was reported, with no minor complications or long-term sequelae. The authors concluded that CMSLT is a feasible approach due to its safety, effectiveness, and patient compliance, emphasizing the precision of the scanner-assisted technology in minimizing thermal damage and improving treatment outcomes. The study's non-randomized design and limited follow-up period suggest moderate evidence strength.

title: Multimodal Deep Learning Prognostic Model for Predicting Treatment Outcomes for Oropharyngeal Carcinoma.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Accurate prediction of locoregional recurrence (LRR) in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is needed to guide treatment de-escalation decisions, but validated prognostic models integrating imaging and clinical data are lacking.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this retrospective multicenter prognostic study, we assembled 1,384 patients with histologically confirmed OPSCC treated with definitive radiotherapy with or without concurrent chemotherapy and without surgical resection of the primary tumor.
analysis.methods: Data were drawn from 1 private institutional archive and five publicly available archives. The primary outcome was LRR. Discrimination was assessed by Harrell Concordance Index (C-index) across 3-fold cross-validation, and risk stratification by Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing. Attribution analysis was used to identify influential predictors.
analysis.main_results: LRR occurred in 161 of 1,384 patients (11.6%) over a median follow-up of 59.8 months (interquartile range, 25.8-89.0 months). The cross-attention model achieved the highest mean C-index, 0.718 (range, 0.699-0.734), followed by the clinical-only (0.705; range, 0.680-0.735), feature concatenation (0.697; range, 0.673-0.721), and imaging-only (0.674; range, 0.666-0.680) models. High-risk patients had significantly shorter LRR-free survival than low-risk patients in all three folds (log-rank P < .001 for each). Smoking history and human papillomavirus status were the most influential clinical predictors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A multimodal cross-attention deep learning model integrating CT with clinical variables showed numerically better discrimination for LRR prediction in OPSCC than unimodal approaches.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform individualized treatment decisions for patients with HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer by improving the accuracy of LRR prediction.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Prospective external validation is required before such models inform individualized treatment decisions.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a validated prognostic model for predicting locoregional recurrence (LRR) in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) by integrating pretreatment computed tomography (CT) with clinical variables. A retrospective multicenter study was conducted using data from one private and five public archives, involving 1,384 patients with histologically confirmed OPSCC. The model, a cross-attention deep learning approach, was compared with clinical-only, feature concatenation, and imaging-only models. The cross-attention model demonstrated the highest mean Harrell Concordance Index (C-index) of 0.718, followed by the clinical-only model (0.705), feature concatenation model (0.697), and imaging-only model (0.674). High-risk patients had significantly shorter LRR-free survival than low-risk patients (log-rank P < .001 for each fold). Smoking history and human papillomavirus status were identified as the most influential clinical predictors. The authors concluded that the cross-attention model showed numerically better discrimination for LRR prediction than unimodal approaches. However, they emphasized that prospective external validation is necessary before these models can be used for individualized treatment decisions.

title: Differences in HPV-related gynaecological malignancies incidence and survival by individual and contextual variables: a population-based study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate differences in the incidence and survival rates of HPV-related gynaecological malignancies, such as vulvar, vaginal, and cervical cancers, by individual and contextual factors like socioeconomic status and stage of diagnosis. Abstract Vulvar, vaginal and cervical cancers are gynaecological malignancies that share a key risk factor: infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a population-based analysis conducted in the Community of Madrid (CM) from 2018 to 2020, focusing on women diagnosed with vulvar, vaginal, and cervical cancers. Data were extracted from the Population-Based Cancer Registry of Madrid (PBCR-CM). As an HPV vaccine is available, many tumours are considered preventable.
analysis.methods: Descriptive analyses were performed to assess sociodemographic and tumour characteristics. Crude, age-specific, and age-standardised incidence rates were calculated. Five-year observed and net survival were computed, with adjustments made using flexible parametric models to evaluate differences in the risk of death by stage.
analysis.main_results: Cervical cancer patients had higher survival rates (71%) compared to those with vulvar/vaginal cancer (50%). Survival was lowest among patients with grade-III and metastatic tumours. Five-year observed and net survival were calculated, globally and stratified by socioeconomic status and stage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the importance of socioeconomic status and tumour stage in influencing survival outcomes among women with HPV-related gynaecological cancers. This study provides an overview of HPV-related gynaecological cancers in CM.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted public health strategies to address disparities in survival rates for HPV-associated cancers, particularly by improving access to care and early detection in lower socioeconomic groups. To address inequalities, PBCR plays an indispensable role by ensuring high-quality epidemiological surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to data from a single region (Community of Madrid) and relies on registry data, which may not capture all relevant contextual factors. The evidence is of moderate strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential for unmeasured confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated differences in the incidence and survival rates of HPV-related gynaecological malignancies, including vulvar, vaginal, and cervical cancers, in women from the Community of Madrid between 2018 and 2020. It focused on how socioeconomic status and tumour stage influenced outcomes. The research used data from the Population-Based Cancer Registry of Madrid (PBCR-CM) and performed descriptive analyses, calculating crude, age-specific, and age-standardised incidence rates, as well as five-year observed and net survival. Results showed that cervical cancer patients had higher survival rates compared to those with vulvar/vaginal cancer, with survival being lowest among patients with grade-III and metastatic tumours. The study emphasizes the role of socioeconomic factors in cancer outcomes and suggests that high-quality epidemiological surveillance is essential for addressing inequalities. However, the study is limited to a single region and relies on registry data, which may not fully account for all contextual variables, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: HPV-driven DNA methylation plasticity reshapes immune regulation in head and neck cancer

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how HPV-driven DNA methylation changes affect immune regulation in head and neck cancer (HNC). The incidence of HPV-related HNC has exponentially increased over recent decades, highlighting the need to explore its impact on tumor biology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on HPV-related head and neck cancer, examining the tumor microenvironment (TME) and immune regulation. It analyzed genome-wide methylation patterns and immune architecture in HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors.
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted genome-wide methylation analysis and characterized immune and stromal compartments, cell–cell interactions, and spatial architecture using high-dimensional single-cell imaging mass cytometry (IMC). Key findings were validated in an external single-cell RNA sequencing cohort.
analysis.main_results: Genome-wide methylation analysis identified 770 differentially methylated positions (P < 0.05, |logFC| <0.20) mapping to 386 genes that distinguish HPV-positive from HPV-negative tumors. These changes were significantly enriched in immune-related pathways.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that HPV-associated DNA methylation reprogramming shapes the spatial and functional organization of the TME in HNC, promoting divergent mechanisms of immune regulation and tumor immune evasion.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the role of HPV-driven epigenetic changes in immune regulation and tumor immune evasion, which could inform future research on HPV-associated cancers and their treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the findings were independently validated in an external cohort, supporting a moderate level of confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how HPV-driven DNA methylation changes influence immune regulation in head and neck cancer (HNC). The incidence of HPV-related HNC has risen sharply, prompting research into its epigenetic effects. Genome-wide methylation analysis and high-dimensional single-cell imaging mass cytometry (IMC) were used to explore immune and stromal interactions in the tumor microenvironment (TME). The results identified 770 differentially methylated positions associated with immune-related pathways, distinguishing HPV-positive from HPV-negative tumors. These findings suggest that HPV-induced epigenetic remodeling alters immune regulation and tumor immune evasion mechanisms. The study's abstract-only nature limits the depth of analysis, but external validation of key findings supports a moderate confidence level. The results may inform future research on HPV-associated cancers and their treatment strategies.

title: HPV Prevalence, Subtype Distribution, and Vaccine-Associated Changes in Fuzhou Women Undergoing Health Examinations: An 11-Year Retrospective Study (2014–2025)

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess long-term trends in Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection rates, subtype distribution, and age-specific patterns before and after HPV vaccination in Fuzhou, China, to inform cervical cancer prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study analyzed 29,041 women (aged 16–79) who underwent HPV genotyping at Fuzhou University Affiliated Provincial Hospital from February 2014 to December 2025. Participants were grouped into pre-vaccination (2014–2017; n=18,542) and post-vaccination (2020–2025; n=10,499).
analysis.methods: Age–infection probability was modeled using restricted cubic spline regression. Using fluorescent microsphere hybridization, 27 HPV subtypes (17 high-risk, 10 low-risk) were detected; overall positivity, high-/low-risk rates, and type-specific prevalence were compared.
analysis.main_results: Overall HPV positivity was 15.77% (15.65% pre vs. 15.97% post; P=0.213). A persistent U-shaped age distribution was observed in both phases, peaking at ≤30 and ≥51 years (nadir 31-40). Post-vaccination, high-risk HPV decreased (14.49%→12.90%; RR=0.89; P<0.001), notably in the 31–40 group (RR=0.79); low-risk HPV increased (5.64% to 7.40%; RR=1.31; P<0.001), especially ≤30 years (RR=2.29).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HPV vaccination in Fuzhou reduced HPV16/18 prevalence, yet rising non-vaccine types (HPV6, HPV81) in young women suggest possible type replacement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Continued molecular surveillance, broader vaccines, and age-specific screening are warranted to address the observed changes in HPV subtype prevalence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on a single center, which may limit generalizability. The evidence is moderate as it relies on observational data without randomized intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This 11-year retrospective study in Fuzhou, China, examined HPV prevalence, subtype distribution, and age-specific patterns in women undergoing health examinations. It found that HPV vaccination reduced high-risk HPV16/18 prevalence, particularly in the 31–40 age group, but also noted an increase in low-risk HPV6 and HPV81 among young women. These findings suggest possible type replacement and highlight the need for continued molecular surveillance, broader vaccine coverage, and age-specific screening strategies. The study's limitations include its retrospective design and single-center setting, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

title: Understanding Cervical Screening Engagement Among Young South Asian Women: Perspectives of Women and Healthcare Professionals.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study aimed to explore barriers and facilitators to cervical screening among South Asian women aged 25-29 in a deprived locality in England, focusing on the declining participation despite increased HPV vaccine uptake.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study used semi-structured interviews with 15 South Asian women and 6 healthcare professionals involved in cervical screening delivery. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Cervical screening engagement among young South Asian women is influenced by cultural, emotional, and structural factors. Limited understanding of HPV and cervical screening, cultural norms around modesty and sexuality, fear of judgment, and structural challenges like appointment access and competing responsibilities were identified as key barriers. Family networks played a dual role as both barriers and facilitators. Healthcare professionals noted the need for culturally responsive communication and flexible service provision to address inequalities in screening uptake.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights a lack of understanding about HPV and cervical screening among South Asian women, even though most have received the HPV vaccine. There is no consensus on the most effective strategies to improve screening engagement, and the evidence is limited to qualitative insights from a single deprived locality in England.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Clear communication about the continued importance of cervical screening should accompany HPV vaccination, especially in areas with low knowledge and awareness. Culturally responsive communication, flexible service provision, and community partnership approaches are recommended to address persistent inequalities in screening uptake.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the declining cervical screening participation among young South Asian women in deprived areas of England, despite increased HPV vaccine uptake. The study used semi-structured interviews with 15 women and 6 healthcare professionals, analyzed via reflexive thematic analysis. Key findings indicate that barriers include limited understanding of HPV and cervical screening, cultural norms around modesty and sexuality, fear of judgment, and structural challenges like appointment access. Family networks act as both barriers and facilitators. Healthcare professionals emphasized the need for culturally responsive communication and flexible service provision to address inequalities. The study suggests that reinforcing cervical screening education alongside HPV vaccination is essential. However, the evidence is limited to a single locality, and there is no consensus on the most effective strategies to improve screening engagement. The findings highlight the need for targeted research and community-based interventions to enhance screening uptake among this population.

title: MmuPV1 and HPV E6 Elevate Nuclear Accumulation of IKKɑ to Impair NF-κB Signaling to Promote Persistent Infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the role of MmuPV1 E6 in disrupting NF-κB signaling, a key pathway in immune regulation, to understand its contribution to persistent infection and cancer development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved analysis of previously published RNA sequencing data and experiments with mouse and human keratinocytes expressing MmuPV1 E6 and its R130A mutant, focusing on the effects of these proteins on NF-κB signaling.
analysis.methods: The researchers analyzed previously published RNA sequencing data and conducted experiments to assess the interaction of MmuPV1 E6 with IKK complex proteins and its effect on nuclear localization of IKKɑ in keratinocytes.
analysis.main_results: MmuPV1 E6 expression was associated with increased nuclear localization of IKKɑ, while the R130A mutant failed to show this increase. Additionally, HPV16 E6 also promoted increased nuclear IKKɑ localization in human keratinocytes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that E6-mediated disruption of NF-κB signaling depends on its interaction with IKK complex proteins and that this mechanism may be conserved between mouse and human papillomaviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms by which HPV E6 proteins disrupt immune pathways, which could inform future research on viral persistence and oncogenesis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on previously published RNA sequencing data and does not include direct experimental validation of the transcriptional changes, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how the E6 oncoprotein of mouse papillomavirus (MmuPV1) interacts with the IKK complex to impair NF-κB signaling, a critical pathway in immune regulation. The research demonstrates that MmuPV1 E6 promotes nuclear accumulation of IKKɑ, which is essential for its ability to disrupt cellular homeostasis and promote persistent infection. The study also reveals that the human papillomavirus HPV16 E6 oncoprotein exhibits a similar effect in human keratinocytes, suggesting a shared mechanism between mouse and human papillomaviruses. These findings highlight the importance of E6-IKK interactions in viral pathogenesis and provide a foundation for understanding how these interactions contribute to oncogenic processes. However, the reliance on existing RNA sequencing data limits the strength of the evidence to moderate, as direct experimental validation of the transcriptional changes was not performed.

title: Preimplementation Factors for a Mobile Decision Support Tool for Cervical Cancer Screening Among Dominican Women Living With HIV: Qualitative Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand barriers and facilitators to implementing a mobile decision support tool for cervical cancer screening among Dominican women living with HIV, given the high risk of cervical cancer in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a secondary qualitative analysis of transcripts from 16 providers and 25 women living with HIV across formative interviews and usability testing in the Dominican Republic.
analysis.methods: The analysis was guided by the Health Equity Implementation Framework and focused on sociocultural, clinic-level, patient, and provider factors that intersected during clinical encounters.
analysis.main_results: Findings indicated that multilevel strategies are necessary for successful initial and sustained implementation of the screening, triage, and treatment protocol.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlighted the importance of addressing societal, clinic-level, patient, and provider factors to ensure the successful implementation of the mobile decision support tool.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that a comprehensive approach is needed to improve cervical cancer screening rates among women living with HIV, emphasizing the need for multilevel strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the secondary nature of the analysis and the potential for bias in the qualitative data, but the evidence suggests a high level of confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study explored barriers and facilitators to implementing a mobile decision support tool for cervical cancer screening among Dominican women living with HIV, emphasizing the need for multilevel strategies to improve screening rates.

title: Intratumoral CD8+ T-cell differentiation is linked to durable HPV-specific immunity after neoadjuvant HPV vaccination with long-acting IL-7 and PD-1 blockade

analysis.research_question_and_background: Durable antigen-specific immunity is a goal of therapeutic vaccination, but its relationship to intratumoral CD8+ T-cell differentiation remains poorly defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We compared anti–PD-1, tirvalimogene teraplasmid (GX-188E), and long-acting IL-7 (GX-I7/NT-I7), alone and in combination, in HPV-positive tumor-bearing mice. We then evaluated the same components in a four-cohort phase 2 neoadjuvant study of 56 patients with resectable HPV-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
analysis.methods: Among tested regimens, triple immunotherapy produced the greatest tumor control and a pooled tumor profile enriched for stemness-associated intratumoral CD8+ states. Post-treatment intratumoral MYC-associated and relative MYC/BATF regulon measures were related to HPV16 E6/E7-reactive activation-induced marker responses at 2 years.
analysis.main_results: In the 11-patient cohort receiving pembrolizumab, GX-188E, and NT-I7, 7 patients had a major pathologic response, including 4 with a pathologic complete response. Paired tumor profiling identified a GZMK+ effector-memory CD8+ state with cytotoxicity- and memory-associated features.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings associate intratumoral GZMK+ effector-memory remodeling with HPV-reactive activation and memory phenotypes 2 years later.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of therapeutic strategies that enhance durable HPV-specific immunity through modulation of CD8+ T-cell differentiation and function.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a phase 2 neoadjuvant trial with a small sample size, and the evidence is based on abstract-only data, which may not fully capture the complexity of immune responses. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between intratumoral CD8+ T-cell differentiation and durable HPV-specific immunity following neoadjuvant vaccination with long-acting IL-7 and PD-1 blockade. Using a combination of mouse models and human clinical data, the research demonstrates that triple immunotherapy significantly improves tumor control and identifies a GZMK+ effector-memory CD8+ state associated with HPV-reactive immune responses. The findings suggest that immune reprogramming through IL-7 and PD-1 blockade may enhance the development of long-term memory T cells against HPV. However, the study is limited to a small phase 2 trial and abstract-only data, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength, highlighting potential avenues for improving therapeutic vaccination strategies against HPV-associated cancers.

title: Same margin, different lesion: margin subtype, glandular involvement, and endocervical curettage status as predictors of residual CIN2+ at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure: An 11-year retrospective cohort study.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study aimed to assess how initial loop electrosurgical excision procedure margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and specimen size relate to re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology and receipt of further surgery.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: In this retrospective cohort study, 287 patients undergoing re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure at a tertiary center (2015-2025) were reviewed. Initial margin status was classified as margin continuity, margin adjacency, or non-evaluable margin. Associations with re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology, residual CIN2+ disease, and receipt of a third surgical intervention were assessed using chi-square/Fisher-Freeman-Halton tests, Cohen's kappa, and multivariate logistic regression.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Initial and re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology showed a significant group-level association (p=0.039) but no case-by-case agreement beyond chance (kappa=-0.009, p=0.754); most patients with initial CIN2/3 had CIN1 at re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure. Margin adjacency independently predicted residual CIN2+ disease at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure (OR 11.045, p=0.049), as did glandular involvement (OR 1.938, p=0.035). Positive margin (OR 333.33, p<0.001) and positive endocervical curettage (OR 41.67, p<0.001) at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure were the strongest predictors of receiving a third surgical intervention.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report on controversies or evidence gaps related to human papillomaviruses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Post-loop electrosurgical excision procedure follow-up should integrate margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and human papillomavirus surveillance rather than rely on margin status alone; genotype-specific differences in human papillomavirus test negativity require confirmation in larger cohorts.

analysis.summary_en: This 11-year retrospective cohort study evaluated how initial loop electrosurgical excision procedure margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and specimen size relate to re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology and further surgical interventions. The study included 287 patients and used statistical methods such as chi-square/Fisher-Freeman-Halton tests, Cohen's kappa, and multivariate logistic regression to assess associations. Key findings indicated that margin adjacency and glandular involvement independently predicted residual CIN2+ disease, while positive margins and endocervical curettage were strong predictors of a third surgical intervention. The study emphasized the need for integrating multiple factors, including human papillomavirus surveillance, into follow-up protocols rather than relying solely on margin status. Genotype-specific differences in human papillomavirus test negativity were noted and require further validation in larger cohorts.
